sources.title: George Fortune, Shona Lexicography (1979)
sources.note: Full original PDF read. Printed p. 22, PDF page 3: nhanga and two meanings, dialect labels. Printed pp. 42 to 44: Hartmann 1894, Elliot 1897, Biehler 1906, spelling and dialect differences. Sample is explicitly later 1974 dictionary entry reproduced in 1979, not nineteenth-century orthography.

sources.title: Nyamushosho and colleagues, Nyanga pottery and the Manyika ethnohistory (2021)
sources.note: Full indexed original article read; direct PMC access challenged. DOI 10.1016/j.heliyon.2021.e 06609. Sections 2 to 4 distinguish Manyika descendants of Mutasa from wider regional usage, primary archival/elder research and specifically twentieth-century pottery accounts (Martin 1941, Stead 1947, Lawton 1965). No projection of every observation into 1878.

sources.title: Martin Prendergast, Iron mining and metallurgy in pre-colonial Zimbabwe (2025)
sources.note: Full 13-page original PDF directly read. Printed pp. 21 to 23: late-nineteenth-century Njanja smelting, air pipes, apprentices, farmers, ore access and markets. Contemporary 1920s demonstration photos not relabeled nineteenth-century photographs. DOI 10.54841/hm.670.

sources.title: Mabgwe and Manyanga, Prehistoric food storage and security in Zimbabwe (2017)
sources.note: Full author-uploaded original chapter read, pp. 223 to 239. Regional communities include Karanga, Kalanga, Venda, Sotho, Tswana and Ndebele; do not assign all bins to one ethnicity. Homba Hills construction/repairs pp. 231 to 233; broad eighteenth/nineteenth-century interpretation and dating limits pp. 235 to 237. No use of internally inconsistent volume estimates. DOI 10.2307/j.ctvh 9 vz 54.15.

sources.title: Nyamushosho and colleagues, Modelling Land Use in the Gold Belt Territories of Iron Age Southern Zambezia (2022)
sources.note: Publisher indexed full text and author-uploaded equivalent read; direct publisher 429. DOI 10.3390/land 11091425; same work RG 363099652. Household section uses ethnographic analogy but specifically cites Bent 1892 p 79 for late-nineteenth-century overnight kitchen accommodation with chicken enclosure at Chief Mugabe homestead.

sources.title: Penias B. Madovi, Food handling in Shona Villages of Zimbabwe (1981)
sources.note: Original article abstract directly read. Sun drying, annual food production and winter shortage of fresh produce. Explicitly 1981 research comparison, not an 1878 ethnography or medical advice.

sources.title: William Beinart, Cecil Rhodes: Racial Segregation in the Cape Colony and Violence in Zimbabwe
sources.note: Full commissioned historical memorandum directly read. Zimbabwe sections:1890 Company settlement, forced labor/taxation/cattle seizure,1896 to 1897 resistance and suppression, deliberate crop/grain destruction. No single unified Shona national army claimed; no uncertain mortality estimate used.

sources.title: University of Johannesburg, Choice of African languages for the University of Johannesburg
sources.note: Institutional language-policy paper, indexed original page 2 checked; direct PDF retrieval failed. Identifies South African Nguni languages isiZulu, isiXhosa, siSwati and isiNdebele. Used for related language grouping, not ethnic uniformity or ancient migration claims.

sources.title: Shadreck Chirikure and Tawanda Mukwende, Colonialism from within versus colonialism from outside (2025)
sources.note: Full original author-uploaded article directly read. DOI 10.1080/0067270 X.2025.2517448, pp. 5 to 7, Old Bulawayo architecture and excavated beads/cattle bones. Do not use its inaccurate claim that Ndebele state succumbed in 1890 or its compressed missionary foundation attribution; only archaeological observations used.

sources.title: Bulawayo City Council, Bulawayo Brief History
sources.note: Institutional original indexed text read; direct fetch failed. Old Bulawayo: Lobengula founded 1870 and resided until 1881. Modern reconstructed iqhugwana distinguished from surviving original structures.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ithunga (milk vessel), 2022.159
sources.note: Primary object catalogue directly read, nineteenth century, northern KwaZulu-Natal, wood and pigment. Carving with spearhead, lugs for traction, movement into mining labor contexts. Raised exterior bands interpreted cautiously; no claim about exact maker or one universal religious practice.

sources.title: Saffron Walden Museum, Southern Africa gallery object guide
sources.note: Primary museum guide directly read,8 PDF pages. Objects 66 to 68 on page 3: late-nineteenth-century northern Nguni girls/women garments; object 101 on page 7 grass-fibre beer strainer,108 ostrich-handled wooden spoon before 1885. Do not extrapolate a single bead-color dictionary, or reproduce erroneous Fort Jameson Malawi attribution elsewhere in guide.

sources.title: Imvo Zabantsundu, 29 December 1884, edited transcription held by UCT Five Hundred Year Archive
sources.note: Four-page edited transcription of original issue directly read. Masthead page 1 title and contemporary English Native Opinion; page 3 Ibala le Cricket, Fear Not and Ethiopian teams,22 November 1884, scorecards; pages 3 to 4 English press notices and advertisements. No claim to have visually inspected original newsprint. This is isiXhosa, one Nguni language.

sources.title: English Heritage, Cetshwayo: King of the Zulus
sources.note: Institutional historical research directly read. War and Exile; London Visit; Return to Zululand. British invasion 1879, Cetshwayo 1882 visit and 1883 return. Does not support a single fall of all Nguni societies.

sources.title: UK Parliament, South Africa: Annexations in Zululand, 19 May 1887
sources.note: Original parliamentary exchange directly read, Hansard vol 315 cols 508 to 509. Redmond questioned how Zulu consent was ascertained; Holland asserted officials reported approval. Treat colonial assertion as attributed statement, not independent proof of consent.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Linguistic/cultural umbrella, not one state. Imported polygon mostly north of Zimbabwe, public warning. No alias with Zimbabwe, Rozwi or Mutapa. Named Hwedza, Great Zimbabwe, Nyanga and Homba Hills examples south of imported minimum latitude. Later 1941/1947/1965 pottery,1974/1979 dictionary and 1981 food observations explicitly dated. Grain bins are regional multi-community comparison, not exclusive ethnicity.

Imported polygon is in Tanzania and cannot locate the southern African linguistic umbrella. Do not substitute Nyamwezi or a particular Ngoni state on geometry alone. Explicit public warning; named Old Bulawayo, KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape examples all outside outline. No aliases to Ndebele, Zulu or Swazi state records. Original sample is isiXhosa in an edited transcription of 1884 newspaper. Different political endings retained, not collective disappearance.
